cards.front: Recall a key point about Separable and Modal Verbs
cards.back: Common separable prefixes: an-, aus-, auf-, ein-, mit-, nach-, vor-, zu-, zurück-, zusammen-, weg-. In subordinate clauses, the prefix stays attached: "...weil ich um 8 Uhr anfange" (NOT anfange ich).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Separable and Modal Verbs
cards.back: "Ich möchte" is technically the subjunctive of mögen but functions as a modal verb. It is the standard way to express "I would like" in German. Note: ich kann, ich muss, ich darf, ich will, ich soll — these all have NO -e ending in the ich form.

cards.front: What should you know about german exam tips — separable and modal verbs?
cards.back: 1. For Separable and Modal Verbs, use a range of vocabulary and complex grammatical structures to access higher marks 2. Check verb tenses, agreements and word order carefully in your written work 3. In translation tasks, translate meaning rather than word-for-word 4. When writing about Separable and Modal Verbs, include opinions and justifications, not just descriptions 5. For listening and reading, focus on key words and cognates to extract meaning
to start/begin (e.g. Ich fange um 8 Uhr an)
to go out (e.g. Ich gehe heute aus)
to come along (e.g. Kommst du mit?)
to come back (e.g. Ich komme morgen zurück)
to get up (e.g. Ich stehe um 7 Uhr auf)
to shop (e.g. Ich kaufe im Supermarkt ein)
